entries.title: AstaBrief: citation-focused SFT and preference training for scientific reports
summary: AstaBrief adapts Qwen3-8B to write cited scientific reports from already retrieved literature snippets in one pass, using citation-filtered supervised examples and agreement-filtered preference pairs.

The released weights and training recipe provide a practical starting point for faster evidence-grounded synthesis, with comparisons limited to the older models and report workflows used during development.

evidence.rationale: The October 2 technical disclosure describes 47K supervised examples and about 6K preference pairs, with citation-density filtering producing the strongest filtering gains. The model card reports citation recall rising from 64.6 for Qwen3-8B to 78.2 for AstaBrief on the 100-question SQABench-CS2 test split. The blog reports 51.1 versus 178.5 seconds across the full Fast/Thinking pipelines, about 3.5 times faster. This is first coverage of the newly published technical write-up; model development largely predates this release. Ai2 and its official mirror date the disclosure October 2 without a verified hour; it is eligible within the 72-hour lookback but conservatively labeled newly-discovered because its position relative to the 10:00 UTC main-window boundary is uncertain.
evidence.limitations: Most training and evaluation occurred in 2025 and were not rerun against current frontier models. Evidence relies heavily on model judges; the human study covers only 14 questions. Pipeline latency compares different workflows, not an isolated model substitution, and citation scores do not fully measure preservation of scientific claim scope. No independent reproduction. Model weights use Apache 2.0, while the verified DPO dataset uses CC-BY-NC-4.0.

entries.title: Make Sparse Rewards Count: Density-Aware Reward Aggregation for Multi-Reward RL
summary: Density-Aware Reward Aggregation increases the weight of objectives that provide useful comparisons in relatively few rollout groups, recalculating these weights for each training batch.

This helps models acquire format and length constraints in fewer optimization steps, offering a practical way to balance multiple rewards while exposing the trade-off between compliance and answer accuracy.

evidence.rationale: Tool-calling and math studies cover 1.5B–7B models, matched baselines, fixed-weight ablations, and held-out evaluation. DeepSeek-R1-7B reaches 95% held-out length compliance at step 50 versus 70 for GDPO. Submission: 2026-09-30T18:45:26Z, after the daily deadline; the cs.CL listing confirms the October 2 public batch. Newly discovered in this run's lookback, with the September 30 original date retained.
evidence.limitations: Fewer optimization steps do not establish wall-clock savings. Stronger length compliance can lower accuracy, and final accuracy leadership varies by model and variant. The exact energy-equalization result assumes ideal normalization and uncapped symmetric weights; it does not directly prove equal policy-gradient contributions for the practical asymmetric variant.

entries.title: Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free
summary: LoopCD guides a looped Transformer's next-token prediction by contrasting its final recurrent state with an earlier state from the same forward pass, requiring no additional training or auxiliary model.
It improves reasoning and code generation in the tested models, while separate multiple-choice experiments show that this guidance can recover accuracy lost by halving recurrent depth.

evidence.rationale: Matched checkpoints, prompts, and recurrent depths across four model families support the decoding effect. Reduced-depth multiple-choice experiments report 22.5–48.2% lower analytic forward FLOPs. Submission: 2026-10-01T17:58:38Z; the cs.LG listing confirms the October 2 public batch. Newly discovered in this run's 72-hour lookback, absent from all 64 previously covered works.
evidence.limitations: FLOPs describe a 512-token prefill calculation, not measured serving speed. Reduced-depth evidence is limited to multiple-choice tasks; guidance strengths and reference states require screening and depend on architecture. Logit guidance adds a readout pass, while hidden guidance can be sensitive to initialization and excessive strength. No public implementation was verified.

entries.title: CATCH: A Controllable Analysis Testbed for Reward Hacking in Coding RL
summary: CATCH evaluates coding reinforcement learning with deliberately vulnerable training rewards and a separate execution audit, allowing researchers to distinguish evaluator exploitation from actual task success.
Its controlled experiments show that monitor-based protection can erode during training, making the testbed useful for studying how safeguards and model behavior adapt to one another.

evidence.rationale: Qwen3-4B experiments vary initialization, reward difficulty, and three mitigation strategies; removing code comments improves monitor recall after training against that monitor. The public repository includes training and audit utilities. Original submission: 2026-09-30T11:36:30Z; the cs.CL listing confirms the October 1 batch. Newly discovered during the 72-hour catch-up search, with original date retained and no prior coverage.
evidence.limitations: Experiments use one 4B model, single-turn synthetic repositories, and deliberately seeded hacking demonstrations. The independent audit covers designed loopholes, not every possible exploit. Initial demonstrations are screened against a related monitor, and the observed suppression-versus-capability trade-offs are not a universal ranking of defenses.

entries.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
summary: AutoCompact trains a coding agent to decide when to summarize its history, preserve a useful working state, and continue consistently from that summary.
Judge-corrected demonstrations followed by task-success reinforcement learning improve repository problem solving even when the original history fits in the context window.

evidence.rationale: Three-run evaluations use one Qwen3-Coder backbone and a shared scaffold on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-PolyBench Verified, reporting 9.2 and 5.0 percentage-point gains over the base agent. Disabling compaction in the same trained checkpoint reduces performance, supporting a contribution beyond weight updates. Newly discovered in this run; its Oct 2 public announcement precedes the main window but falls within the 72-hour lookback.
evidence.limitations: Evidence covers one model and coding tasks. Inference costs are token-price estimates excluding training and judge-guided data collection; summary-quality checks use keyword screening with manual spot checks. No code or checkpoint link was found in the inspected primary publication, and results were not independently reproduced.

entries.title: From Knowledge Access to Source Learning: Developing Source-Specific Competence
summary: SourceLearn builds a persistent representation of a document collection, repository, or API source and revises it through self-directed study and feedback from earlier tasks.
Reconstructing revisions from the original source helps agents reuse organized knowledge on later tasks while retaining direct retrieval for precise evidence.

evidence.rationale: Five benchmarks and three backends use disjoint guidance/test tasks; the authors report the highest score among tested methods in 13 of 15 settings. Ablations and a four-source matched-context comparison support benefits beyond added context alone. Newly discovered during this run from the Oct 2 announcement batch, within the 72-hour lookback.
evidence.limitations: Task-guided refinement uses reference answers, and main comparisons add source-model context; matched-budget controls cover a subset. Grounding audits still find unsupported claims, and gpt-oss-120b regresses on AppWorld. The linked repository contains only LICENSE and a minimal README; the project page could not be retrieved. No independent reproduction.

entries.title: Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents
summary: Component Routing divides a GUI agent's experience into interface locations, procedures, state facts, and lessons, then chooses whether each belongs in model weights or retrieved context.
A rule based on recurrence and dependence on the current state offers a practical way to combine fine-tuning with memory instead of sending every experience through the same route.

evidence.rationale: Paired held-out tests span three 7–8B model families, MobileGym and AndroidWorld, and three seeds, with deterministic task checkers. Routing improves over the better single destination by 3.5 percentage points on average. Inspected but deferred in the Oct 2 run; first inclusion uses newly-discovered because its Oct 2 public release is within this report's lookback and it has never been published here.
evidence.limitations: The route rule is calibrated on a narrow set of GUI models and extracted components, with structured-state or accessibility matching. Some component contrasts include zero, and routing does not beat the best single destination in every configuration. Code and data are described as a future release; no independent reproduction.

entries.title: RapidMoE: Exploiting Cross-Asymmetry via Adaptive Residual Offloading for Large-Scale MoE Inference
summary: RapidMoE combines low-precision expert computation on GPUs with selectively higher-precision CPU work, using residual weight representations and importance-based routing to balance the devices.
This reduces duplicated host-memory storage and offloading stalls when serving large mixture-of-experts models on memory-limited CPU–GPU systems.

evidence.rationale: Screened October 2 and fully reviewed for this catch-up selection: v1 is October 1 at 08:02:24 UTC; the October 2 announcement list and official schedule imply public release at October 2 00:00 UTC. A800/RTX 4090 tests cover DeepSeek-R1/V3 and Qwen3-235B; the authors report up to 3.5x decoding speedup over KTransformers, with accuracy checks, component ablations, and a 1,000-request serving workload.
evidence.limitations: Serving tests use concurrency four and 0.2 requests/s; accuracy varies slightly against the Q4 reference. Calibration takes hours and performance depends on CPU memory bandwidth and hardware balance. These results do not establish high-concurrency cluster performance; no public RapidMoE implementation was verified.

entries.title: Building a High-Performance and Portable vLLM Linear Backend with Helion
summary: This vLLM backend uses Helion to automatically tune quantized matrix multiplications for individual input shapes, switching between tuned kernels and existing implementations at runtime.
It offers a more compact way to optimize decoding kernels while translating some kernel-level improvements into higher serving throughput.

evidence.rationale: The page's publication metadata and official RSS agree on October 2 at 19:55:07 UTC, inside the main interval. The authors report 1.110–1.178x geometric-mean kernel speedups across tested comparisons and over 10% serving-throughput gains for some workloads, using an H100 80GB, dense Qwen models, three 8-bit formats, and ShareGPT. The linked fork includes kernels, configurations, and tuning instructions.
evidence.limitations: Helion runs under CUDA Graph replay for at most 32 tokens; larger shapes fall back to existing kernels. Tests disable prefix caching and do not establish cross-hardware portability. The integration is a separate fork, and additional models require offline tuning that can take hours; results were not independently reproduced.

entries.title: GPU-Initiated Communication: Dissecting Down to the Bone
summary: This study uses minimal transports and production libraries to separate GPU-driven network costs from queue management, synchronization, and CPU-proxy overhead.
Its measurements explain how batching, queue isolation, and resource pressure affect fine-grained mixture-of-experts communication, helping engineers choose and tune transports for their workloads.

evidence.rationale: Screened October 2 and fully reviewed now: v1 is October 1 at 09:46:08 UTC; the October 2 announcement list and official schedule imply October 2 00:00 UTC availability. Controlled tests span H100, H200, B200, and GB200 with payload validation and network counters. The authors find that queue isolation reduces loaded latency and dormant communication code can reduce kernel throughput; benchmark sources and raw results are accessible.
evidence.limitations: This is a transport-mechanism study, not an end-to-end LLM speedup claim. Latency commonly uses median measurements on one pinned node pair, while platforms differ in CPUs, links, firmware, and providers. Small-message findings depend on traffic, clock state, completion semantics, and library configuration; no results were independently reproduced.

entries.title: Universal Byte-Level Encoding: UTF-8/UTF-16 Routing to Reduce Cross-Script Token-Budget Disparities
summary: Universal Byte-Level Encoding routes characters between UTF-8 and UTF-16 before standard byte-pair encoding, reducing the initial encoding cost for several scripts while preserving exact decoding.
It can reduce multilingual token-budget disparities and fit more content into a fixed context window, particularly with compact vocabularies and poorly covered scripts.

evidence.rationale: Matched tokenizer-data comparisons span 204 language-script configurations, Unicode round-trip audits, and language models from 182M to 1.3B. The 101-language/32K setting reduces token-premium Gini by 9.4%; language-model quality differences are small and mixed. arXiv v1: 2026-10-01T16:26:10Z, within this report's interval. The timestamp above is submission time; the arXiv cs.CL listing separately confirms the October 2 public announcement batch.
evidence.limitations: Changing vocabulary requires retraining or adaptation rather than swapping into an existing checkpoint. Some languages regress, the largest token savings include scripts outside the downstream training corpus, and three-seed results do not establish improved language-model loss parity.

entries.title: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)
summary: TESS learns a reusable data-selection network by matching per-example loss differences between ordinary and validation-guided models, avoiding a weighting objective that can suppress most examples and favor shortcuts.
It transfers selection from a smaller sample to unseen instruction data, offering a way to target fine-tuning data without relearning a separate weight for every example.

evidence.rationale: A selector trained on 50K Tulu V2 examples is applied to 197K candidates before Llama-2-7B fine-tuning; math/code task-average performance is 26.46 versus 21.54 for random selection. Loss ablations and cross-dataset probes support transfer. arXiv v1: 2026-10-01T17:23:29Z. The timestamp above is submission time; the arXiv cs.CL listing separately confirms the October 2 public announcement batch.
evidence.limitations: Task-specific validation examples and representation/gradient features are required. Evidence uses a limited set of older model families and tasks; the safety experiment measures harmful-data identification, not improved safety. Code release is promised upon acceptance rather than verified as available.

entries.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
summary: HC-DLM couples a continuous latent plan with repeatedly decoded tokens that guide the next denoising step, allowing token decisions to be revised throughout generation.
The design improves controlled planning and reasoning tasks at small scale, offering evidence that latent planning and token-level feedback can complement one another in diffusion models.

evidence.rationale: Component ablations and matched 6M-parameter comparisons support the coupling: hard-Sudoku accuracy is 72.41% versus 70.73% for reproduced CCDD, and longer Countdown improves from 25.35% to 37.52%. A separate 118M sampling-model experiment evaluates short unconditional text. arXiv v1: 2026-10-01T17:59:39Z. The timestamp above is submission time; the arXiv cs.CL listing separately confirms the October 2 public announcement batch.
evidence.limitations: Evidence remains at moderate scale; reported sampling parameter counts exclude embeddings and the training-only encoder. Natural-language comparisons use external-model generative perplexity, different tokenizers, and historical baselines; the autoregressive baseline still scores better, and reported training times are not hardware-controlled speed comparisons.

entries.title: Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval
summary: Causal Memory Policy randomizes a few retrieval slots so memories that the normal retriever misses can still have their effect on a specific answer measured.
This provides a diagnostic for biased memory-utility estimates, while showing that accurate per-query measurements alone do not tell an agent what to retain for future questions.

evidence.rationale: Inspected the intervention design, estimator assumptions, benchmark comparisons and explicit limitations. LongMemEval experiments improve required-memory discrimination from 0.542 to 0.664 AUC, with additional analyses on LoCoMo, multi-hop QA and Mem0.
evidence.limitations: The main identification demonstration uses a candidate pool constructed with knowledge of required memories; tested deployable selectors fail to recover that pool reliably. Exposure consumes context and the work makes no effective retention-policy claim. The linked anonymous code page yielded no readable content; not independently reproduced.

entries.title: VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks
summary: VeriHarness uses the generator's own model to resolve disagreements between candidate outputs and challenge claims that all candidates share, checking both against files and other environmental evidence.
It then selects or revises the deliverable with a traceable record of checks, improving verification without requiring a stronger judge model.

evidence.rationale: Full protocol, matched ten-rollout pools, three-seed verification results and ablations were inspected across five workspace benchmarks and two models. The authors report higher selection scores than the tested baselines in all ten model–benchmark settings.
evidence.limitations: Results depend on ten candidate rollouts per task and accessible environmental evidence; shared errors still survive. Revision adds compute, some comparator costs are estimated, and verification prices do not represent the full generation-plus-verification cost. Model/rubric grading remains part of several benchmarks; no independent reproduction.

entries.title: Finding the Right Fit: Model-Harness Interactions across Agent Tasks
summary: This study compares 66 model–harness configurations across terminal and professional-work benchmarks and finds that model rankings and preferred harnesses change with the task.
The released adapters and scored trajectories help developers evaluate a complete agent configuration instead of assuming that a model ranking transfers unchanged to their runtime.

evidence.rationale: Inspected the common task sets, configuration matrix, cost accounting and matched-trajectory analysis. The study covers five models, four configurable harnesses and two native pairings, with 6,204 scored runs and a verified public code repository.
evidence.limitations: One counted run per task leaves run-to-run variance unmeasured. Native settings, tools and budgets are not uniformly matched, so comparisons do not isolate individual components; task subsets are not upstream leaderboard reproductions. Explanations from a few trajectory pairs remain hypotheses; not independently reproduced.

entries.title: Introducing Olmo-core 3: Open, scalable training infrastructure for large MoEs
summary: Olmo-core 3 keeps mixture-of-experts weights resident on GPUs and combines expert and pipeline parallelism with a distributed optimizer, GPU-resident routing, and low-precision execution.
The open stack offers a practical way to increase total expert capacity without repeatedly gathering weights, with throughput gains demonstrated against Ai2's earlier training implementation.

evidence.rationale: The full October 1 engineering blog and linked repository were inspected. A preliminary 47B-model test on eight B300 GPUs reports 52,000 versus 19,400 tokens/second/GPU against the previous FSDP stack; separate experiments test expert-count scaling and MXFP8. The publisher supplies a date without an exact time.
evidence.limitations: Performance is author-reported and configuration-specific. Trillion-parameter results use random routing or short capacity tests, not trained-model quality or sustained convergence. The linked technical report exceeded the retrieval tool's size limit, so this entry relies on the full engineering blog rather than claiming paper review.

entries.title: MegaFlux: Skew-Resilient MoE Megakernels via Pipelined Expert Replication
summary: MegaFlux dynamically replicates heavily used experts and overlaps replica transfers and gradient reductions with computation inside a mixture-of-experts megakernel.
It reduces stragglers caused by uneven routing, making fused expert execution more useful when a few experts attract disproportionate work.

evidence.rationale: Catch-up discovery: v1 was submitted September 30 at 20:09:09 UTC but is in the October 2 announcement list, consistent with scheduled public release at October 2 00:00 UTC. Eight-B200 experiments include controlled routing sweeps and pipelining ablations; DeepSeek-V4-Pro prefill in vLLM reports 1.13–1.26x median batch-latency speedups over fixed expert placement on 160 LongBench-Pro prompts.
evidence.limitations: Layer sweeps use synthetic operands and trace-derived routing distributions, with spare memory for replicas. Small skewed backward workloads can slow down, and tests cover one NVLink domain rather than cross-node deployment. The end-to-end measurement stops at first-token production; no MegaFlux code release was verified.

entries.title: Leto: Fast In-Place Recovery for LLM Training on Surviving Hardware
summary: Leto retains recoverable model state outside a failed training process and prepares a shadow process on the same hardware, using protected memory and transactional updates to resume consistently.
For failures that leave accelerators usable, this avoids checkpoint reloads and repeated training work, reducing the time otherwise spent recovering idle GPUs.

evidence.rationale: Catch-up discovery: v1 was submitted September 30 at 20:29:57 UTC but appears in the October 2 announcement list; the official schedule implies October 2 00:00 UTC public release. On 6- and 72-A100 testbeds, five model workloads recover in 6–19 seconds, reported as 3.6–6.5x faster than their best checkpointing baseline; fault-injection tests also check recovery consistency.
evidence.limitations: The fast path requires hardware-operable failures; fatal failures still use checkpoints. Measurements inject failures, and very large cluster claims are simulations. Protection and shadow processes add overhead, including a small regression when all failures are fatal; a public Leto implementation was not verified.

entries.title: ePACT: Energy-Performance-Aware Commitment Tracking for LLM Serving
summary: ePACT adjusts active serving replicas and GPU clocks using feedback on hourly energy targets and predictions of request deadlines.
It helps operators balance latency with contracts that penalize both overuse and underuse of a committed energy volume, rather than optimizing consumption alone.

evidence.rationale: v1 was submitted October 1 at 14:32:24 UTC and appears in the October 2 announcement list, consistent with scheduled availability at October 2 00:00 UTC, inside the main interval. Physical one-hour tests use 32-GPU H20/H200 pools; full-day profile-based simulations report 73.8%/75.7% lower modeled deviation cost than fixed-capacity vLLM while preserving similar deadline attainment.
evidence.limitations: The cost is a weighted deviation metric, not an electricity bill or total energy reduction. Full-day results are simulated, energy excludes the rest of the facility, and the positive underuse penalty does not apply to every contract. Prediction checks do not guarantee deadlines; code was not verified.

entries.title: How Much Is an AI Token Worth? Scaling Laws for Wild AI-Generated Web Text
summary: The authors train hundreds of small language models on mixtures of human and detector-labeled AI web text, then fit scaling laws that distinguish AI text's saturating benefit from its potential harm.
The results motivate tracking human and AI validation losses separately and choosing data mixtures according to the target distribution and available human data.

evidence.rationale: Across 800 runs from 19.9M to 973M parameters, the paper tests data-budget and mixture effects and extrapolates fits from models up to 268M. Its fitted law predicts held-out human-text loss better than the compared laws. arXiv v1: 2026-09-30T17:50:22Z, within this report's interval. The timestamp above is submission time; the arXiv recent-submissions listing separately confirms the October 1 public announcement batch.
evidence.limitations: English web pretraining and next-token loss dominate the evidence; detection labels can be imperfect and the authors include detector-company researchers. Results do not establish that curated synthetic data or frontier-scale models follow the same tradeoff; forecast compute penalties are model-based projections.

entries.title: Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR
summary: GRAFT replaces a learner's entirely unsuccessful rollout groups with informative groups from a peer model, controlling policy mismatch through compatibility weighting and clipped updates.
This lets heterogeneous models learn from complementary discoveries without a designated stronger teacher, and stored peer trajectories can retain much of the benefit.

evidence.rationale: Three model pairs and five math benchmarks show average gains of about 2.1 points over eight-rollout GRPO; ablations test gating and group replacement. arXiv v1: 2026-09-29T15:47:25Z. Newly discovered through the September 30 discovery index during this delayed run, within the 72-hour lookback and absent from prior reports. The timestamp above is submission time; the arXiv recent-submissions listing separately confirms the September 30 public announcement batch.
evidence.limitations: Experiments use two-model pairs of at most 3B parameters on verifiable math. Gains depend on complementary successes, cross-tokenizer weights are compatibility proxies rather than exact density ratios, and paired-training compute should not be presented as a single-model cost reduction.

entries.title: PivotOPD: Learning to Recover from Pivotal Mistakes in Multi-Turn Agents
summary: PivotOPD uses a teacher to locate consequential mistakes and name corrective actions, then distills a hint-conditioned copy of the student at both mistake and recovery turns.
This supplies learning signals where unsuccessful rollouts provide little reward feedback, helping agents recover instead of merely reducing the probability of a wrong action.

evidence.rationale: Matched training budgets, 13 baselines, three seeds, and held-out ALFWorld, WebShop, and search-QA tests support the method; both 1.7B and 8B students improve benchmark averages, with additional coding-agent transfer. arXiv v1: 2026-09-30T17:48:11Z, within this report's interval. The timestamp above is submission time; the arXiv recent-submissions listing separately confirms the October 1 public announcement batch.
evidence.limitations: Later recovery turns require exact environment replay, which live websites may not support. Teacher action errors become incorrect training targets; pivot detection agrees with the ALFWorld oracle within one turn on 77.8% of failures, so supervision remains imperfect.

entries.title: Learning from Research: Toward Lifelong Agent Harness Evolution
summary: ScholarEvolve turns ideas from research papers into changes to an agent's tools, context, skills, memory, and workflow, then evaluates combinations of those changes.
It broadens the improvement strategies available to a fixed model and demonstrates how newly retrieved research can guide successive harness revisions.

evidence.rationale: Inspected module construction, validation/test separation, three-run results and cumulative ablations on AppWorld and Tau2-Bench Telecom. Reported Qwen3.5-27B AppWorld Challenge completion rises from 49.6% to 63.6%; a separate three-window experiment studies continued research-driven updates.
evidence.limitations: Evidence covers two task backbones and two environments. Matching search rollout allocation does not match every research/coding cost; individual tasks still regress and evidence-coverage failures persist. The paper's linked GitHub repository was empty when checked, so implementation availability is unverified; no independent reproduction.

entries.title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization
summary: Turbo Harness trains a small editor to adapt an existing agent harness to each task, using a playbook distilled from earlier successful and failed harness changes.
A single editor call produces a task-specific code patch, offering a way to improve a fixed execution model without running a fresh harness search for every request.

evidence.rationale: Methods, held-out splits and ablations cover seven benchmarks; repeated coding and terminal evaluations support improvements over the corresponding global harness. The playbook and editor training are complementary in the reported ablation.
evidence.limitations: Benefits depend on an existing search archive and additional training rollouts. Coding tests hold out issues within selected repositories; reported execution costs exclude offline search and the per-instance editor call, so they do not establish total-cost savings. Results were not independently reproduced.

entries.title: OSWorld-Science: A Benchmark of Computer Use Agents for Learning and Using Scientific Software
summary: OSWorld-Science evaluates computer-use agents on 146 scientific-software tasks, checking application state and artifacts such as molecular structures, segmentation masks, and numerical results.
Its shared harness and partial-credit evaluators make it useful for separating incomplete scientific workflows from valid deliverables and studying where current agents fail.

evidence.rationale: Inspected task construction, executable evaluators, common interaction protocol, 12-model results and trajectory analysis. The benchmark spans seven domains, and the public repository provides the evaluation runtime and links to task data.
evidence.limitations: Task coverage is uneven: four software configurations account for 58.2% of tasks. Scores include partial credit, not only full completion; the 23-task harness ablations have one run per cell and no comparison survives the stated multiple-testing correction. Software licensing and environment requirements constrain replication; not independently reproduced.

entries.title: HAPMoE: Heterogeneity-Aware Automatic Parallelism Planning for Mixture-of-Experts Models Training
summary: HAPMoE profiles accelerator and communication costs, then jointly chooses parallelism, uneven pipeline partitions, device placement, and recomputation for mixture-of-experts training.
It generates runnable Megatron-LM plans that use mixed accelerator clusters more effectively without manually tuning each distributed-training configuration.

evidence.rationale: Catch-up discovery: v1 was submitted September 30 at 09:11:46 UTC and is in the October 1 announcement list, consistent with scheduled availability at October 1 00:00 UTC. Across 16–32-device heterogeneous MoE configurations, the authors report geometric-mean throughput of 1.67x and 1.78x Megatron-Infinigence for two Mixtral-style models, with adapted competing planners and ablations.
evidence.limitations: Plans are fixed from warm-up profiles and cannot adapt online to changing routing or device availability. Tests cover limited model and cluster configurations; larger networks may add contention and failure effects. The comparison includes adapted rather than original competing systems, and no public implementation was verified.

entries.title: Vosti: Specifying, Implementing, and Verifying Deterministic LLM Inference
summary: Vosti combines a formally verified inference engine with checked GPU-kernel contracts so batching, prompt chunking, and cache reuse preserve identical output logits under a fixed deployment configuration.
It provides a foundation for reproducible serving and debugging when scheduling changes would otherwise alter a model's numerical behavior.

evidence.rationale: Catch-up discovery: v1 was submitted September 30 at 04:58:09 UTC and appears in arXiv's October 1 announcement list; the standard announcement schedule implies October 1 at 00:00 UTC availability. The authors verify engine invariants and kernel contracts and report 5,488 matching logit comparisons across seven Llama/Gemma models, with performance measured on one H200.
evidence.limitations: The proof establishes determinism, not model correctness or cross-hardware reproducibility, and trusts compiler/runtime boundaries. Vosti is slower than default serving modes and SGLang's deterministic mode in the evaluated synthetic sessions; its performance advantage is relative to vLLM's invariant modes on decode-heavy workloads.

entries.title: Taming Speculative Search for Test-Time Scaling in LLM Serving
summary: SpecScale prunes uncompetitive reasoning branches early, shares computation between identical prefixes, and batches process-reward verification across requests.
These scheduling changes reduce wasted speculative work and improve the capacity of a server running verifier-guided beam search for multiple users.

evidence.rationale: Catch-up discovery: v1 was submitted September 30 at 09:04:53 UTC and appears in the October 1 announcement list, consistent with scheduled availability at October 1 00:00 UTC. Four generator configurations and three mathematics datasets are tested on one A100 80GB; eight-beam MATH experiments report 1.51x/1.43x throughput over non-speculative search for Qwen2.5-3B/7B, alongside component ablations and accuracy checks.
evidence.limitations: Results concern small mathematics generators with separate reward models on a custom serving framework, not general production reasoning. FastTTS is partially reimplemented with two resource-constrained scheduling features omitted; verification thresholds require profiling, accuracy changes vary, and no SpecScale code destination was verified.

entries.title: Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision
summary: LIFT trains language models to carry a latent state across generated tokens, using a teacher's next-token distributions to supervise this feedback channel while preserving parallel pretraining.
Its controlled language-modeling and procedural-task gains suggest a way to improve learning efficiency and state tracking without expressing every intermediate computation as text.

evidence.rationale: Sections 3-5 and Appendix F provide architecture, ablations, and token/compute comparisons at 135M, 350M, and 1B non-embedding parameters; compute matching includes teacher forward passes. The main three-scale experiment reports 5-5.5% lower perplexity at matched tokens. The arXiv v1 submission was 2026-09-29T17:57:40Z, within the daily interval.
evidence.limitations: Only the smallest language-model scale has three training seeds; larger runs have one. Main evaluations use sequential prompt processing, while parallel prefill trades extra passes for quality; results are not uniformly better than vanilla Transformers across every compute-matched setting.

entries.title: From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation
summary: MAESTRO lets a stronger teacher briefly take over a student's reasoning during on-policy distillation, using teacher-student disagreement to choose when and how long to intervene.
In small-model math experiments, this selective guidance improves accuracy while shortening training rollouts, providing a practical alternative to fixed teacher intervention.

evidence.rationale: Ablations and eight mathematical benchmarks use Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B students and a 4B teacher. The 1.7B student's macro-average accuracy is 47.12%, versus 45.18% for Relay-OPD and 41.23% for OPD; authors report 67.3% shorter training responses than OPD. The arXiv v1 submission was 2026-09-29T13:06:14Z, within the daily interval. First seen records the earliest saved baseline source check; full text, previously inaccessible, was reviewed for this daily report.
evidence.limitations: Evidence is confined to two small students, one teacher, and math. Shorter responses are a token metric, not demonstrated equivalent wall-clock or total-cost savings after teacher scoring and intervention overhead.

entries.title: Correct Answers, Invalid Traces: What Verifiable Grade-School Math Reveals About Chain-of-Thought Traces
summary: Using mechanically verifiable synthetic math, the authors show that models can produce correct answers with invalid reasoning traces even after training exclusively on valid solutions.
The work motivates checking trace semantics under distribution shift when evaluating reasoning or designing oversight, since answer accuracy alone does not establish trace validity.

evidence.rationale: The study trains 124M models and checks syntax, arithmetic, and semantic dependencies on 4,096 problems per difficulty level. At the hardest out-of-distribution level, 31.6% of correct answers have invalid traces; altered-supervision experiments probe this separation. The arXiv v1 submission was 2026-09-29T17:46:55Z, within the daily interval. First seen records the earliest saved baseline source check; full text, previously inaccessible, was reviewed for this daily report.
evidence.limitations: A synthetic, small-model study with seed sensitivity does not establish failure rates for frontier-model monitoring. The authors explicitly distinguish trace validity from causal faithfulness and do not test adversarial concealment or an operational safety monitor.

entries.title: Addendum to GPT-6 Astra System Card: GPT-6.1 Sol
summary: OpenAI pairs GPT-6.1 Sol's release with evaluations of coding, computer use, factuality, and agent alignment, reporting improved capability and task cost relative to GPT-6 Sol.

The evaluation package provides a current case study for comparing useful task performance with failure disclosure, permission compliance, and monitoring behavior instead of treating capability gains as a guarantee of safer agents.

evidence.rationale: The September 29 system card describes adversarial evaluations and matched deployment simulations: among 49,650 internal tasks, the authors report 28 severity-3-or-higher flags for GPT-6.1 Sol versus 42 for GPT-6 Sol. The accompanying release report specifies benchmark versions and reasoning settings for capability-cost comparisons.
evidence.limitations: These are developer-reported evaluations, not independent reproduction or a disclosed training recipe. Internal simulations may not transfer to external deployment, evaluation awareness and model versions affect comparisons, and some safety categories regress despite aggregate improvement. The publisher provides a date, not a precise publication time.

entries.title: ContextRender: From Execution Dependencies to Agent Context
summary: ContextRender keeps complete tool results in a persistent graph and selects what the agent sees using observed value reuse, recency, and relevance.
This gives long-running agents a way to reduce repeated context costs while retaining omitted information for later recovery, with competitive task performance under a 6K history budget.

evidence.rationale: Full methods, matched-budget baselines and ablations inspected; three models on AppWorld and 8-objective QA. Reports better task performance than five managed-context baselines across nine settings and 10.2–32.2% lower standardized inference cost than full history. The arXiv v1 submission was 2026-09-29T14:57:00Z, within the daily interval.
evidence.limitations: Costs use a common pricing/cache model and only tasks triggering context management; they are not measured provider-bill savings. Performance is below full history in two settings. Reuse detection is exact, case-sensitive value matching; no independent reproduction or verified code release.

entries.title: SelfSearch: Reward-Free Search for Self-Improving Agents
summary: SelfSearch lets a fixed-weight agent revise its instructions, tools, and execution code using records of earlier self-improvement attempts, without downstream benchmark rewards during search.
The resulting tools transfer to coding and terminal tasks, offering a way to improve an agent without repeatedly paying for benchmark evaluation during candidate generation.

evidence.rationale: Inspected search protocol, result tables, ablations and evaluation settings. Final population-mean success improves in all six model-family/benchmark settings; record-removal and fixed-improver ablations support the proposed mechanisms. The arXiv v1 submission was 2026-09-29T16:36:24Z, within the daily interval.
evidence.limitations: Tests use 120 SWE-bench Verified tasks, 60 multilingual tasks and 89 Terminal-Bench tasks, with two lineages per model configuration; independent-search consistency is unestablished. Reward-free excludes downstream scores, not local execution/check feedback. Evaluation remains a separate cost; no verified public code release.

entries.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
summary: Anthropic evaluates GLM-5.3's autonomous cybersecurity capabilities in isolated benchmarks and separately tests whether its safeguards resist malicious requests in simulated environments.
The findings illustrate why successful task execution and resistance to misuse need distinct measurements when assessing powerful tool-using models.

evidence.rationale: The September 29 report describes automated and human-assisted tests, with 50 successful end-to-end exploit attempts out of 410 on ExploitBench and a separate 100-task internal evaluation. Its safeguard experiment uses 50 samples per condition and explicitly measures engagement rather than successful real-world attacks.
evidence.limitations: A model developer evaluates a competitor; some data and evaluation machinery are internal. Safeguard trials use an LLM-simulated shell that executes no code, and access conditions differ between released weights and guarded APIs. Results are author-reported and should not be generalized to real-world attack success rates; only a publication date is supplied.

entries.title: SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving
summary: SPLASH changes attention parallelism while requests are running by reusing resident weights and KV caches, transferring missing state in the background, and switching at a batch boundary.
This lets serving systems adapt to changing concurrency and context lengths; its additional ownership layout stores attention weights and each request's cache without replicating either.

evidence.rationale: arXiv v1 was submitted 2026-09-29 at 14:02:29 UTC, inside the daily window. The SGLang-based implementation compares four layouts on B200, H200, and DCU; the authors report 1.3–1.73x throughput versus fixed layouts on B200/GLM-5.3 and measure all twelve switch directions.
evidence.limitations: Main experiments use fixed output lengths and controlled concurrency sweeps. Switching needs memory headroom and pre-captured graphs; transfers contend for bandwidth, and short-lived workload changes may not repay the cost. Speculative decoding and heterogeneous workers are outside the implementation scope.

entries.title: Mixture-of-Kittens: MoE Megakernel for NVL72s
summary: Mixture-of-Kittens fuses expert dispatch, expert computation, and result combination into a deterministic GPU kernel, choosing communication direction per operator and avoiding CPU synchronization.
It targets NVL72 systems where conventional mixture-of-experts communication schedules leave performance unused, providing an open implementation for overlapping computation and data movement.

evidence.rationale: Newly discovered within the 72-hour catch-up window, absent from the baseline; arXiv v1 was submitted 2026-09-28 at 18:22:34 UTC. Alongside layer benchmarks and ablations, a 512-GB300 comparison changes only the MoE backend and reports 1,070.2 versus 761.0 tokens/second/GPU, a 41% training-throughput increase.
evidence.limitations: The full-model result comes from the authors' internal production stack and one reported configuration; the open layer benchmarks use synthetic routing inputs. Gains vary with precision, token count, and expert parallelism, and should not be generalized to other accelerator fabrics or training convergence.

entries.title: Purlin: Separating Orchestration from the Datapath of Collectives
summary: Purlin separates collective operations into layout specifications, a reusable coordination protocol, and hardware-specific data-movement primitives.
This makes communication easier to specialize across GPU generations while improving distributed inference when collective latency is a substantial part of request time.

evidence.rationale: Newly discovered in the 72-hour catch-up window: arXiv v1 was submitted 2026-09-29 at 07:57:27 UTC, before the main window opened. Tests use eight-GPU A100, H200, and B200 servers; the authors report a 1.13x geometric-mean offline serving gain across 135 configuration–baseline comparisons, with microbenchmarks and quality checks.
evidence.limitations: The largest online gain occurs under overload rather than sustainable service at that arrival rate. MSCCL++ wins in some high-concurrency cases, NCCL leads some large variable-length reductions, and strongly imbalanced collectives remain unevaluated; all results are author-reported.

entries.title: It's All Training: A Fully Synthetic Single-Stage Recipe for LLMs
summary: SYNTH turns curated Wikipedia seeds into grounded questions, reasoning traces, and varied tasks, allowing small language models to acquire instruction-following behavior within a single training stage.
Controlled data ablations make it a useful reference for testing whether carefully generated synthetic data can improve learning efficiency and targeted factual recall.

evidence.rationale: Sections 3-5 describe generation and matched 600M-model data ablations; the authors report an 11-17 point advantage over their post-trained web-data controls across the aggregate task groups.
evidence.limitations: Knowledge is bounded by roughly 58,000 seed articles, language coverage is shaped by English sources, and experiments target small models; token savings are not equivalent to total savings once teacher generation is counted.

entries.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
summary: Kimi K3 combines hybrid recurrent and latent attention, attention across residual layers, and a sparse expert architecture in a native multimodal model with 2.8 trillion total parameters and 104 billion activated parameters.

Its public report connects architecture, data, optimization, and long-context post-training, providing a current reference for how several efficiency improvements support scaling a large open-weight model.

evidence.rationale: The August 7 revision includes architecture equations, scaling-law experiments, training schedules, and evaluation settings; Section 3.2 reports approximately 2.5x overall scaling efficiency relative to Kimi K2 on held-out validation data.
evidence.limitations: The efficiency result combines multiple changes and is not an isolated architectural gain; the authors state that overall performance trails their strongest proprietary comparators, and released weights do not make the full training process reproducible.

entries.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
summary: Kimi K2 introduces MuonClip, which adds query/key weight clipping to Muon so that attention logits remain controlled during large-scale mixture-of-experts training.
It is a practical optimization reference because it links a specific instability mechanism to an intervention used in a trillion-parameter training run.

evidence.rationale: The optimizer algorithm, mid-scale instability experiment, and Appendix D ablations accompany the authors' report of training on 15.5 trillion tokens without observed loss spikes.
evidence.limitations: This is an established recipe component, not a current model ranking; the trillion-parameter evidence is author-reported, and the intervention needs attention-specific adaptation and threshold choices.

entries.title: Olmo 3
summary: Olmo 3 releases an end-to-end model development pipeline with separate pretraining, targeted mid-training, context extension, and post-training stages, together with data and intermediate checkpoints.
Its short continuation experiments and integration tests provide a reproducible way to choose data mixtures and measure capability tradeoffs before committing to a full training run.

evidence.rationale: The April 14, 2026 paper revision documents stage-level comparisons, data filtering, continuation ablations, and domain tradeoffs; public code and checkpoints make it a useful open training reference.
evidence.limitations: Recipe development focuses on 7B and 32B models, with substantial compute requirements; improvements on one data domain can reduce performance on others, and release-time leadership claims are not treated as current rankings.

entries.title: Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension
summary: OlmPool holds data and context-extension procedures fixed across 26 comparable models to test how normalization, grouped-query attention, sliding windows, and pretraining context length affect later long-context ability.
The results show why a context-extension recipe should be validated on the intended architecture early, since ordinary short-context metrics can miss substantial downstream weaknesses.

evidence.rationale: The full report provides paired architectural comparisons and HELMET, RULER, and long-context perplexity results, with model configurations and before/after checkpoints released. Its publication date is corroborated by the linked Ai2 author announcement dated April 23, 2026; the inspected report front matter is undated.
evidence.limitations: The controlled suite centers on approximately 7B dense models and one data/extension setup; these findings do not establish that the same architectural choices are universally harmful at other scales or training budgets.

entries.title: LoRA Without Regret
summary: This experimental study examines when low-rank adaptation can match full fine-tuning by varying adapter rank, training-set size, batch size, learning rate, and the layers being adapted.

It gives practitioners a concrete recipe for efficient adaptation, including sufficient adapter capacity and coverage of feed-forward layers, while identifying large-data and large-batch regimes where gaps remain.

evidence.rationale: The report sweeps rank and learning rates on Llama and Qwen models using instruction and reasoning data, and separately tests mathematical reinforcement learning.
evidence.limitations: Supervised comparisons primarily use log loss rather than broad downstream generation metrics; the findings apply to tested post-training regimes and do not guarantee equivalence for pretraining-like data volumes.

entries.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
summary: Direct Preference Optimization converts a regularized preference-learning objective into a direct loss on preferred and rejected responses, avoiding a separately trained reward model and online policy rollouts.
It remains a useful foundational baseline for aligning model behavior from offline preference pairs with a comparatively simple training pipeline.

evidence.rationale: The paper derives the objective and evaluates sentiment control, summarization, and single-turn dialogue against reinforcement-learning and supervised baselines; an author reference implementation is available.
evidence.limitations: Its preference-model assumptions and dependence on offline data matter; the original experiments do not establish universal superiority to online RL or robustness under distribution shift.

entries.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
summary: DeepSeek-R1 demonstrates large-scale reasoning training with group-relative policy optimization and verifiable rewards, while separating a pure-RL experiment from a staged recipe that improves response usability.
It supplies a foundational reference for eliciting reasoning from a strong pretrained model and transferring those capabilities to smaller models through distillation.

evidence.rationale: The January 4, 2026 revision describes rewards, training stages, reasoning evaluations, and failure modes; the published model family enables follow-up study but the original training run was not reproduced here.
evidence.limitations: Reliable verifiers are central, model-based rewards can be exploited, and the reported model has overthinking, language-mixing, structured-output, and tool-use limitations; this is a foundational recipe rather than a current leaderboard claim.

entries.title: On-Policy Distillation
summary: On-policy distillation lets a student generate its own trajectories and uses teacher token probabilities to provide dense feedback on the states the student actually visits.
The report demonstrates a practical route to improving reasoning and restoring instruction-following after domain training without rebuilding an entire reinforcement-learning reward pipeline.

evidence.rationale: The author report supplies reverse-KL pseudocode, reasoning and personalization experiments, and a linked implementation; its June 2026 note documents replacement models in the maintained recipe.
evidence.limitations: Teacher quality and token-probability access are prerequisites; some cost comparisons use extrapolated supervised baselines, and the cookbook's replacement models do not themselves reproduce the original numerical results.

entries.title: s1: Simple test-time scaling
summary: s1 combines supervised training on a small curated reasoning dataset with budget forcing, which controls when a model stops or continues its thinking at inference time.
Its simple open implementation separates training quality from inference-time computation, making it a useful baseline for studying the accuracy and cost tradeoff of longer reasoning.

evidence.rationale: The March 1 revision includes data-selection ablations, decoding comparisons, and compute-versus-accuracy curves; the authors report AIME 2024 accuracy increasing from 50% to 57% under budget forcing.
evidence.limitations: The principal evidence comes from a small set of math and science benchmarks; gains eventually flatten and are bounded by context length, so more thinking is not a guarantee of more reliable answers.

entries.title: Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal
summary: This work uses interpretable model features to identify which concepts preference data rewards or suppresses before optimization, then connects those signals to targeted data and training interventions.
It offers a way to debug unwanted changes such as safety regressions and excessive stylistic habits at their training source instead of relying only on aggregate scores after training.

evidence.rationale: The June 11 revision tests feature-based predictions against observed training changes and compares intervention protocols; the reported feature-conditioned prediction fit reaches R-squared 0.9 in the studied setup.
evidence.limitations: Concept extraction and correlations constrain what can be diagnosed; the paper observes off-target effects for several interventions, so interpretability does not provide a general guarantee of safe post-training.

entries.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
summary: ReAct alternates reasoning, environment actions, and observations so an agent can revise its plan using external evidence.
It remains a useful foundation for tool-using agent loops because task execution and information gathering become part of the reasoning process.

evidence.rationale: The ICLR camera-ready paper compares reasoning-only, acting-only and interleaved policies on question answering, fact verification and interactive tasks; its ablations and failure analysis make the control pattern inspectable. The arXiv history records v1 on October 6, 2022 and v3 on March 10, 2023.
evidence.limitations: This is a foundational method, not a claim of current benchmark leadership. Retrieval failures and repetitive loops remain possible; ReAct alone trails chain-of-thought on the reported HotpotQA setting.

entries.title: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
summary: This work separates task execution from a controller that assesses accumulated work, proposes next steps, evaluates their value, and dispatches workers using persistent artifact memory.
It offers a way to spend larger inference budgets more effectively on long tasks by choosing which partial results to reuse, repair, or abandon.

evidence.rationale: Sections 3, 5 and 6 provide the controller design and matched-worker comparisons across four benchmarks and three models; reported ProgramBench performance is 71.5% with GPT-5.5 versus 58.0% for Codex. Submission history verifies September 29, 2026 at 17:57:25 UTC.
evidence.limitations: A new preprint with no independent reproduction here. Equal model-call allowances do not equal token, latency or FLOP budgets; control overhead hurts at small budgets, and the design underperforms direct control on the LongCoT-mini chess subset.

entries.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
summary: SWE-agent builds a model-oriented interface for repository search, file editing, and test execution, with concise feedback and checks that help agents recover from mistakes.
It establishes interface design as a practical source of coding-agent improvements and supplies an open implementation for studying tool ergonomics.

evidence.rationale: The paper's Table 3 isolates editing, search, file-viewing and context choices; its GPT-4 Turbo setting resolves 18.0% of SWE-bench Lite versus 11.0% for a shell-only agent. The arXiv history records v1 on May 6, 2024 and v3 on November 11, 2024; the code repository is accessible.
evidence.limitations: Historical results use older models, task sets and per-instance budgets and should not be interpreted as a current coding leaderboard. Better interfaces reduce specific errors but do not ensure successful repair.

entries.title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
summary: Qwen-UI-Agent combines screenshots, command execution, and API results in one action space, with batched actions and training across simulated environments and physical phones.
This broadens computer-use agents toward workflows that mix mobile, browser, and desktop interaction while reducing some unnecessary model turns.

evidence.rationale: The report details the action space, environment construction, long-trajectory training and evaluation. Authors report 82.1% on MobileWorld, 92.2% on MobileWorld-Real and 79.5% on OSWorld-Verified; the arXiv history verifies July 30, 2026 at 13:58:41 UTC.
evidence.limitations: These are author-reported benchmark results, not independently reproduced rankings. Real-phone evaluation uses AutoJudge, which reaches 92.8% agreement on 666 expert-reviewed examples; parts of the larger-model training and environment release remain future work.

entries.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
summary: Anthropic describes a context-management approach that combines selective retrieval, conversation compaction, persistent notes, and separate subagent contexts.
These patterns help long-running agents retain decisions and recover relevant information without carrying every prior observation in the active prompt.

evidence.rationale: The dated September 29, 2025 engineering article explains concrete implementations in Claude Code, including retrieving by lightweight references and preserving unresolved work during compaction. It is selected as an implementation reference for working context and memory.
evidence.limitations: This is engineering guidance with product examples, not a controlled comparison establishing the best memory algorithm. Compression can discard critical details, and runtime retrieval adds latency.

entries.title: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
summary: Search-R1 trains language models to alternate reasoning with search queries, using answer-level rewards and masking retrieved passages out of the policy loss.
It provides an open recipe for learning when and how to obtain external evidence instead of relying only on a fixed retrieval step before answering.

evidence.rationale: The inspected v5 paper specifies interleaved rollout generation, retrieval-token masking and comparisons on seven general and multi-hop question-answering datasets; code and checkpoints are linked from the accessible repository. The first submission is March 12, 2025 and the inspected revision is August 5, 2025.
evidence.limitations: The reported gains concern the tested models, retrieval setup and answer-scoring protocol. They do not establish general web-research reliability, source trustworthiness or resistance to malicious retrieved text.

entries.title: Shockingly Simple Self-retrospection Improves Agentic Models Without RL
summary: Retrospection-Only Fine-Tuning trains an agent on its own explanations of attempted tasks while leaving the action trajectory as context rather than a prediction target.
This suggests a route to learning from failed as well as successful experience without a reward-based policy update, with improvements demonstrated on coding tasks.

evidence.rationale: The paper gives the online training procedure, GRPO comparisons and behavioral ablations. Its no-verifier Qwen3.5-4B run reaches 49.2% SWE-bench Verified and 26.8% Pro after 20 updates versus 48.0% and 25.3% for GRPO after 40; submission history verifies September 28, 2026 at 17:54:24 UTC.
evidence.limitations: A new preprint primarily studying software engineering with Qwen3.5-4B; the mechanism is not causally established across domains. The method lacks independent semantic validation of self-generated explanations, and measured update/time efficiency is not a universal total-compute claim.

entries.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
summary: Anthropic describes an orchestrator-worker research system in which a lead agent delegates independent searches and synthesizes compact findings from separate subagent contexts.
The report offers concrete practices for task boundaries, effort allocation, tool design, evaluation, and recovery when building parallel research agents.

evidence.rationale: The June 13, 2025 article explains the architecture and observed coordination failures, backed by internal research evaluations and production experience. Its reported 90.2% improvement concerns an Opus 4/Sonnet 4 multi-agent configuration against single-agent Opus 4 on an internal research evaluation.
evidence.limitations: Internal evaluation data do not establish a public leaderboard result or isolate coordination from additional compute. The article reports much higher token use and cautions that tightly coupled work is less suited to parallel agents.

entries.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
summary: This harness separates initial environment setup from repeated implementation sessions, using a feature list, progress records, version history, and end-to-end tests to preserve continuity.
It gives builders a concrete pattern for making incremental progress across context resets and detecting premature completion.

evidence.rationale: The November 26, 2025 article connects observed long-running coding failures to specific harness mechanisms and supplies an accessible autonomous-coding example. The source explains initialization, session recovery and browser-based verification.
evidence.limitations: The demonstration targets full-stack web development and is not a broad controlled benchmark. Generalization to other domains and the best division of work between agents remain open; browser-tool limitations still leave verification gaps.

entries.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
summary: A builder agent extracts reusable support principles from development-task feedback and converts them into task-specific tools, context, memory, and execution controls for another agent.
The method explores improving an agent's environment without changing either model's weights, turning prior failures into reusable harness-design knowledge.

evidence.rationale: Methods, resource limits and held-out evaluation are described in the paper and appendices. Authors report an 8.95-point macro-average gain over no-skill construction across Harness-Bench and NewtonBench; submission history verifies September 29, 2026 at 17:55:56 UTC.
evidence.limitations: A new preprint whose generalization evidence is within the studied benchmarks; learning and construction costs fall outside target execution limits. The linked repository could not be retrieved, and the paper also describes a future full-code release, so no accessible code artifact is claimed.

entries.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
summary: AgentDojo provides an extensible environment for testing whether tool-using agents complete legitimate tasks while resisting instructions embedded in untrusted tool results.
It makes the security-versus-utility tradeoff measurable and supplies reusable tasks, attack surfaces, and defense baselines for agent evaluations.

evidence.rationale: The paper defines user and attacker goals across 97 tasks and 629 security test cases and evaluates defenses, including tool filtering. The accessible repository supports extension; arXiv records June 19, 2024 for v1 and November 24, 2024 for the inspected v3.
evidence.limitations: The original scores concern historical models and the included environments, not current deployment security. Tool filtering can fail when required tools also enable an attack; the original suite does not cover continuing user tasks with an unreset context.

entries.title: Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models
summary: Failure-Transparent Agents isolates a reporting problem by giving models fixed failed-tool traces and checking whether subsequent claims are supported by the available evidence.
Its structured evidence contract offers a concrete design to test when reducing false completion claims, while preserving useful recovery advice.

evidence.rationale: The benchmark includes 100 synthetic blocked tasks and 3,600 human-annotated responses across six models; authors report pooled false-success rates of 22.8% for baseline and 0.8% with the contract. Submission history verifies September 28, 2026 at 17:51:41 UTC.
evidence.limitations: A new preprint measuring response fidelity after fixed failures, not end-to-end execution or recovery. The contract bundles multiple changes, the additional model cohort is post-confirmatory, and independent double annotation or inter-annotator agreement is not reported.

entries.title: Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters Using Megatron-LM
summary: Megatron-LM combines tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, using interleaved pipeline stages and communication optimizations to distribute very large models across GPU clusters.
It provides a foundational framework for choosing a parallelism configuration by balancing model memory, communication, and time spent waiting between pipeline stages.

evidence.rationale: The SC 2021 paper analyzes parallelism and microbatch tradeoffs, then benchmarks training iterations for models up to one trillion parameters on as many as 3,072 A100 GPUs; component experiments examine communication and pipeline scheduling.
evidence.limitations: These are historical systems measurements, not current hardware rankings or proof that a trillion-parameter model was trained to convergence. The best configuration depends on cluster topology, model shape, and batch size.

entries.title: DCP: Addressing Input Dynamism In Long-Context Training via Dynamic Context Parallelism
summary: Dynamic Context Parallelism partitions attention into small blocks and replans their placement for each batch's sequence lengths and attention masks.
It reduces unnecessary cross-GPU communication and balances variable-length workloads, making long-context training more efficient when static parallelism wastes resources.

evidence.rationale: The paper provides a hypergraph-based planner, execution design, attention microbenchmarks, and end-to-end 8B-model experiments on 64 A100 GPUs; reported training speedups reach 1.16x for causal masks and 1.46x for sparse masks.
evidence.limitations: The causal-mask range includes 0.94x slowdowns; benefits depend on sequence variability, mask sparsity, planning resources, and communication overlap. Public implementation was not verified.

entries.title: AReaL: A Large-Scale Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning System for Language Reasoning
summary: AReaL separates rollout generation from policy updates so workers can keep producing and consuming training data without waiting for the longest response in a batch.
Staleness control and a modified policy objective help retain learning quality while improving GPU utilization, providing an open reference for asynchronous reasoning-model reinforcement learning.

evidence.rationale: The authors evaluate mathematical and code reasoning across 1.5B–32B models and ablate policy staleness and interruptible generation; the original experiments report up to 2.57x throughput versus synchronous configurations.
evidence.limitations: The gains depend on balancing generation and training; short generations can reduce the advantage, and excessive policy staleness still harms learning. Results are author-reported and software-version specific.

entries.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
summary: PagedAttention stores key-value caches in dynamically allocated blocks, allowing vLLM to avoid large contiguous reservations and share cached state across related sequences.
More efficient memory use permits larger concurrent batches, making this a foundational open reference for high-throughput language-model serving.

evidence.rationale: The paper details cache management, scheduling, preemption, and distributed execution, with OPT and LLaMA experiments on A100 GPUs using ShareGPT- and Alpaca-derived workloads plus block-size ablations.
evidence.limitations: The original comparisons use historical FasterTransformer and reimplemented Orca baselines with synthetic arrival times. Block size trades memory fragmentation against kernel efficiency; the paper does not rank current serving releases.

entries.title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
summary: SGLang combines a programming interface for multi-call language-model workflows with a runtime that reuses prompt prefixes through RadixAttention and accelerates constrained decoding.
This reduces repeated prefill work and exposes parallelism in agent, retrieval, and structured-output applications, making it a useful open serving reference.

evidence.rationale: The revised paper studies 7B–70B language models and multimodal workloads on A10G/A100 hardware, with component ablations and cache-hit measurements that explain the observed improvements.
evidence.limitations: The historical comparison uses vLLM 0.2.5 and other older baselines; its headline speedup is not a ranking of current engines. Long-output workloads with little shared context show much smaller gains.

entries.title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
summary: DistServe runs prompt prefill and token decoding on separate GPUs and independently chooses their resource allocations and parallelism.
It increases the number of requests served within both first-token and per-token latency targets, establishing a practical foundation for disaggregated inference.

evidence.rationale: The OSDI work evaluates OPT-13B/66B/175B across chat, code, and summarization workloads on 32 A100 GPUs, with bandwidth-aware placement and ablations of the disaggregation design.
evidence.limitations: Results use historical engines, synthetic arrival times, and workload-specific latency targets. KV transfers need sufficient bandwidth, and the prototype leaves advanced preemption and fault tolerance to future work.

entries.title: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference
summary: LMCache makes KV caches reusable across requests and inference engines through a separate storage layer, optimized transfers, and a standardized connector.
It lets serving systems trade GPU memory and repeated prefill computation for CPU or remote storage while also supporting prefill-decode disaggregation.

evidence.rationale: The revised report evaluates CPU offload, remote storage, and disaggregated serving with multiple open models on H100 hardware, including real-trace-derived workloads and transfer-level ablations.
evidence.limitations: Cache reuse depends on exact shared context and available bandwidth; remote retrieval can be slower than recomputation. Reported gains depend on the compared engine versions, and SGLang's native CPU offload performs similarly in one tested configuration.

entries.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression
summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer cache reuse, sparse attention, FP4 KV storage, and approximate replay of sliding-window states to shrink long-context memory.
Its encoder-decoder design also reduces prefill work, targeting the memory, storage, and bandwidth costs of input-heavy agents with up to one million context tokens.

evidence.rationale: The report explains cache layout and replay mechanics and reports 890 bytes per token for global GPU-resident KV, roughly one quarter of DeepSeek-V4-Flash, with persistent cache around one eighth of that baseline.
evidence.limitations: These are architecture-specific author measurements, not universal savings. Bounded replay reconstructs approximate states; the authors identify uncharacterized robustness risks at cache-resumption boundaries and in sparse long-context retrieval.

entries.title: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
summary: FlashAttention-4 redesigns attention pipelines for Blackwell GPUs, overlapping matrix operations with softmax while reducing shared-memory traffic and other non-matrix overhead.
The CuTe-DSL implementation provides an open example of how attention algorithms and kernels must adapt when compute throughput grows faster than supporting hardware.

evidence.rationale: B200 BF16 attention benchmarks span 1K–32K sequences, causal and noncausal masks, and several head dimensions; the authors report up to 1.3x over cuDNN 9.13 and 2.7x over the tested Triton baseline.
evidence.limitations: These are attention-kernel measurements, not full-model training speedups. The paper explicitly notes that newer cuDNN releases incorporated similar techniques and achieved comparable performance; gains are hardware- and shape-specific.

entries.title: Towards Full Pipeline FP8 Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
summary: This study traces instability in FP8 reinforcement learning to quantization errors that distort policy-update clipping and prevent undesirable outputs from receiving corrective gradients.
Its Calibrated Clipping method periodically uses BF16 reference statistics to adjust clipping bounds, making low-precision rollout and training more stable across the tested reasoning models.

evidence.rationale: GRPO and DAPO experiments cover 8B–32B Qwen models and multiple FP8 scaling granularities, with controlled analyses of entropy surges and recovery toward BF16 performance.
evidence.limitations: Periodic calibration requires two BF16 shadow forward passes. Reported 1.1–1.5x throughput measurements isolate offline training and exclude calibration, so they do not establish end-to-end RL speedups; some accuracy gaps remain and code was not verified.

entries.title: 6x faster Async Checkpointing in PyTorch, using Cached Plans, no GIL contention
summary: PyTorch distributed checkpointing moves background saving into a separate process and reuses save plans to reduce Python lock contention and expensive metadata collectives.
These changes keep checkpoint persistence from depressing training throughput for as long, making frequent recovery checkpoints more affordable at large GPU counts.

evidence.rationale: Meta and Crusoe report a Llama-3-70B/TorchTitan run on 1,856 H200 GPUs where background checkpoint processing fell from about 436 to 67 seconds, with GPU-to-CPU staging taking about 0.78 seconds.
evidence.limitations: The 6.5x figure concerns background checkpoint processing, not overall model training. Benefit depends on storage, checkpoint structure, and repeated plans; initial planning and coordinator metadata remain costs.

entries.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
summary: This infrastructure study connects DeepSeek's mixture-of-experts architecture, low-precision execution, and communication needs to the design of its GPU cluster and multi-plane network.
It provides a concrete reference for reasoning about how accelerator features, interconnect topology, and model design jointly determine training and serving efficiency.

evidence.rationale: The authors analyze a 2,048-H800 deployment, compare network topologies, and describe bandwidth contention, expert communication, and hardware constraints alongside deployment measurements.
evidence.limitations: Some proposals are future hardware recommendations rather than implemented improvements. Cost estimates and topology conclusions depend on the studied cluster; current NIC limitations require extra intra-node forwarding for cross-plane traffic.
